question.problem:
A particular shop sells watermelons and melons. The weight of a watermelon is normally distributed with a mean of $10\,\text{kg}$ and a standard deviation of $4\,\text{kg}.$ The weight of a melon is normally distributed with a mean of $5\,\text{kg}$ and a standard deviation of $2\,\text{kg}.$ If one watermelon and one melon are randomly selected, what is the probability that the weight of the watermelon is more than $3$ times greater than the weight of the melon? You may assume that the weights are independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.7088\,$ | $\,0.7123\,$ | $\,0.7157\,$ | $\,0.7190\,$ | $\,0.7224\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7422\,$ | $\,0.7454\,$ | $\,0.7486\,$ | $\,0.7517\,$ | $\,0.7549\,$ |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7734\,$ | $\,0.7764\,$ | $\,0.7794\,$ | $\,0.7823\,$ | $\,0.7852\,$ |

current_example.problem:
The math test results of a group of students are normally distributed with a mean of $67$ and a standard deviation of $12.$ The results of the same group on a history test are normally distributed with a mean of $73$ and a standard deviation of $9.$ If one student is randomly selected, what is the probability their combined score from both tests is more than $150?$ You may assume that the student's scores on both tests are independent. 

*Hint: A table of values of $\Phi(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $\Phi(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\, 0.05 \,$ | $\, 0.06 \,$ | $\, 0.07 \,$ | $\, 0.08 \,$ | $\, 0.09 \,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\, 0.5 \,$ | $\, 0.7088 \,$ | $\, 0.7123 \,$ | $\, 0.7157 \,$ | $\, 0.7190 \,$ | $\, 0.7224 \,$ |
| $\, 0.6 \,$ | $\, 0.7422 \,$ | $\, 0.7454 \,$ | $\, 0.7486 \,$ | $\, 0.7517 \,$ | $\, 0.7549 \,$ |
| $\, 0.7 \,$ | $\, 0.7734 \,$ | $\, 0.7764 \,$ | $\, 0.7794 \,$ | $\, 0.7823 \,$ | $\, 0.7852 \,$ |
current_example.worked_solution:
Let $X$ denote the student's math test result, and let $Y$ denote the student's history test result. We want to find 

$$
P( X+Y > 150).
$$

Since $X$ and $Y$ are  independent random variables such that $X\sim N(67,12^2)$ and $Y\sim N(73,9^2),$ then 

$$
\begin{aligned}X+Y & ∼N(67+73,{12}^{2}+{9}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(140,225).\end{aligned}
$$

 
So, the variable $X+Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu = 140$ and standard deviation $\sigma = \sqrt{225} = 15.$

In order to find $P(X+Y > 150),$ we convert $X+Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X+Y>150) & =P(Z>\frac{150-140}{15}) \\  & ≈P(Z>0.67) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 0.67) \\  & =1-Φ(0.67)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
\Phi(0.67 )\approx 0.7486.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X+Y>150) & ≈1-Φ(0.67) \\  & ≈1-0.7486 \\  & =0.2514.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that the probability that the combined score is more than $150$ is $0.2514.$
